# Ares Security LLC

> Ares Security is a minority woman-owned security guard company based in Colorado Springs, Colorado, founded in 2021. It provides licensed and bonded armed and unarmed security officers, access control, restricted-area escort, relief and surge coverage, and mobile patrol for federal, commercial, industrial, and institutional sites across Colorado: the Front Range (Colorado Springs, Denver, Fort Collins, and Pueblo), the Western Slope (Grand Junction, Glenwood Springs, Montrose, and Durango), and Alamosa and Trinidad in the San Luis Valley and the south. Federal agencies can order through its GSA Multiple Award Schedule, contract 47QSMS25D009Q.

Key facts, each checkable on the linked pages:

- Ownership and certifications: minority woman-owned; SBA Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB250470); WBENC certified Women's Business Enterprise (WBE2303571); Denver M/WBE and SBE certified; Colorado Verified Diverse Business and Colorado Verified Small Business.
- Federal identifiers: GSA MAS 47QSMS25D009Q (SIN 561612), NAICS 561612 (Security Guards and Patrol Services), UEI XQXDN6E33SF4, CAGE 9KL18. Active on SAM.gov through March 26, 2027. Eligible for WOSB set-aside awards under NAICS 561612.
- Licensing: Colorado has no statewide security license; cities license security companies. Ares holds city licenses in Colorado Springs (0850744L), Denver (2021-BFN-0001984), and Pueblo (26422), and is an approved armed and unarmed training provider in each. Ares holds a business license in Glenwood Springs, Durango, and Trinidad, the sales and use tax license that serves as Fort Collins’ business license, and a contract security license in Alamosa; Grand Junction and Montrose require no license for a security company, as each city confirmed.
- Service area: statewide in Colorado, ready to staff ten cities: Colorado Springs (headquarters, ZIP 80906), Denver, Fort Collins, and Pueblo on the Front Range; Grand Junction, Glenwood Springs, Montrose, and Durango on the Western Slope; and Alamosa and Trinidad in the San Luis Valley and the south.
- Record: under 1% missed shifts since 2021; across five past performance evaluations, clients rated Ares Very Good or Exceptional on 43 of 45 criteria, none below Satisfactory; its longest client has kept it on post continuously since 2022, through multiple renewals; employees rate it 4.8 out of 5 on Indeed.
- How posts are staffed: a member of Ares leadership trains each officer on the post and works the first shift on every new post; on-call coverage is written into every contract. Armed officers are firearms-qualified by Ares's veteran NRA-certified firearms instructor. Supervisors include veterans.
- Federal experience: access control, escort, and vehicle inspection for restricted areas on military installations, alongside base security forces.
- Contact: 719-696-3966, contact@aressecurity.co. Careers: careers@aressecurity.co.

## Services

- [All security services](https://aressecurity.co/services): Armed and unarmed officers, access control, restricted-area escort, and relief coverage for federal, commercial, and industrial sites across Colorado.
- [Armed Security Officers](https://aressecurity.co/services/armed-security-officers): Licensed, firearms-qualified armed security officers across Colorado, from Denver to Grand Junction. Trained on post by leadership. Order through GSA MAS.
- [Unarmed Security Officers](https://aressecurity.co/services/unarmed-security-officers): Uniformed and plainclothes unarmed security officers for lobbies, perimeters, and public areas across Colorado, from the Front Range to the Western Slope.
- [Access Control Officers](https://aressecurity.co/services/access-control): Access control officers for Colorado sites: credential checks, visitor screening, and gate, dock, and lobby control, with logs you can audit.
- [Restricted-Area Escort](https://aressecurity.co/services/restricted-area-escort): Restricted-area escort for crews, visitors, and deliveries in Colorado: people and vehicles verified, every escort in line of sight, and custody logs.
- [Mobile Patrol](https://aressecurity.co/services/mobile-patrol): Mobile patrol in Ares-marked patrol cars across Colorado: after-hours checks and multi-property routes with time-stamped reports.
- [Relief & Surge Coverage](https://aressecurity.co/services/relief-surge-coverage): Relief shifts, overflow posts, and surge staffing for site owners, primes, and guard companies anywhere in Colorado, so a call-out never empties a post.

## Industries

- [Government & Defense](https://aressecurity.co/industries/government-defense): Officers for federal agencies, military bases, and defense contractors in Colorado, through GSA MAS 47QSMS25D009Q, and security escorts for crews on base.
- [Commercial & Retail](https://aressecurity.co/industries/commercial-property): Security officers for Colorado stores, grocery, shopping centers, banks, hotels, and offices: loss prevention, access control, and armed posts.
- [Critical & High-Liability Sites](https://aressecurity.co/industries/critical-infrastructure): Security for data centers, utilities, hospitals, cash-handling, and other high-liability sites in Colorado: access control, armed posts, and logs.
- [Institutional & Community](https://aressecurity.co/industries/institutional-community): Security officers for apartments, HOAs, schools, campuses, community health centers, and places of worship across Colorado.
- [Construction, Industrial & Logistics](https://aressecurity.co/industries/construction-industrial): Construction and industrial site security in Colorado: gate control, perimeter rounds, and after-hours coverage for builds, yards, and warehouses.
- [Airport & Transportation](https://aressecurity.co/industries/airport-transportation): Security officers for airport-area sites, transit and parking facilities, and cargo operations in Colorado: credential checks, gate control, and logs.

## Guides for buyers

- [Insights](https://aressecurity.co/insights): Plain answers for people buying security in Colorado: choosing coverage, contracting through GSA, city licensing, and what to expect on post.
- [What an access control officer does, and when a site needs one](https://aressecurity.co/insights/what-does-an-access-control-officer-do): What an access control officer does, why badges and card readers are not enough, when a site needs a staffed post, and the REAL ID rules at federal sites.
- [What prime contractors look for in a small-business security subcontractor](https://aressecurity.co/insights/what-primes-look-for-security-subcontractor): What prime contractors check before naming a small-business security subcontractor: subcontracting goals, set-aside limits, verifiable status, and staffing.
- [Escorts for contractors on military bases: how they work](https://aressecurity.co/insights/contractor-escorts-military-bases): Who may escort contractors on a DoD installation, what an escort does on a shift, and what to line up before a crew mobilizes on a Colorado base.
- [How to choose a security company in Colorado](https://aressecurity.co/insights/how-to-choose-a-security-company-colorado): What to check before hiring a security company in Colorado: the city license, insurance, who the officers work for, call-out coverage, and red flags.
- [How much do security guards cost in Colorado in 2027?](https://aressecurity.co/insights/security-guard-cost-colorado): Security guard costs in Colorado for 2027: minimum wages ($15.71 state, $19.84 Denver), what a 24/7 post costs in pay alone, and what drives the price.
- [Who covers the post when an officer calls out?](https://aressecurity.co/insights/relief-surge-coverage): Every security roster runs short sometimes. What to line up before a call-out, an inspection, or a contract change leaves a post empty.
- [Armed or unarmed security: how to decide](https://aressecurity.co/insights/armed-or-unarmed-security): Most sites need unarmed officers; some need armed ones. How to decide: what the officer may have to stop, and what the contract, insurer, and law require.
- [What a security post order is, with an example](https://aressecurity.co/insights/what-is-a-post-order): What a security post order is, what “post” means, a sample post order outline with an example entry, and paper versus electronic post orders.
- [Construction site security checklist](https://aressecurity.co/insights/construction-site-security): A construction site security checklist for Colorado builds: the gate, the perimeter, after hours, each phase, and escorts and access on federal sites.
- [Buying security through a GSA Schedule](https://aressecurity.co/insights/buying-security-through-gsa): How agencies order security through a GSA Schedule: finding SIN 561612 holders on eLibrary, wage determinations on orders, set-asides, and vendor checks.
- [Security guard licensing in Colorado: what each city requires](https://aressecurity.co/insights/colorado-security-licensing): Colorado has no statewide security license. What Colorado Springs, Denver, Pueblo, and other cities require of security companies and officers.
